_written: 2026-10-10, AFTER gen32/33 (no signal improvement accepted), BEFORE any gen34 number was computed.
idea: TWO-SPEED pipeline. A failed challenge costs only the fee; a lost funded account costs the payout stream. So the challenge can be run at higher risk (faster, more failures, rebuy) and the funded account at lower risk. Objective = money per unit of time, not per attempt.
signals: frozen E2 (src/qpl/strategies/cft_e2.py), no change. Challenge strategy S_c in {LIQUID2 (BTC+ETH), MAJ10 (10 Binance majors)}; funded strategy always LIQUID2.
pipeline simulation: from a start date, repeat for 730 days: buy a challenge (fee), trade it at (S_c, v_c) until pass or fail (no time limit); if failed buy the next one the next day; if passed run funded at (LIQUID2, v_f): every 30 days withdraw 0.80 x 0.95 x profit if equity > start and reset; on a funded breach go back to buying challenges. Equity-based daily loss on real daily lows (all simultaneous), same rules for funded as for the program.
metrics: net = payouts - fees over 24 months (fraction of account size); months to first funded; attempts used; P(net > 0)
selection: per program: (S_c, v_c, v_f) maximising mean net on historical starts 2018-01-01..2020-12-31 (every 5 days) with returns truncated at 2022-12-31
evaluation: historical starts 2023-01-01..2024-10-08 (to data end 2026-10-08) and block bootstrap (2000 paths of 730 days, mean block 20 days, joint rows of both strategies' daily (net, worst, best) at all risk levels from 2018-2026)
gate 'BETTER' (vs gen31 single-speed pol: evaluation-period mean net higher AND median months to first funded lower AND bootstrap mean net higher AND bootstrap P(net > 0) >= 0.70
trials: risk/policy layer only: 2 x 6 x 3 = 36 policies per program; signals unchanged (alpha trials stay 121)
caveats: CFT fees/payout rules UNCERTAIN; assumes challenges can be re-bought immediately and funded rules equal challenge rules; parallel accounts not modelled
